project-built-ins-and-porch.html.title: Built-ins & Porch
project-built-ins-and-porch.html.lede: Small spaces, high detail: a slate built-in with matching wainscot, and a porch floor painted in a diamond pattern.
project-built-ins-and-porch.html.facts: <dt>Location</dt><dd>Greater Burlington</dd><dt>Type</dt><dd>Residential, interior and porch</dd><dt>Surfaces</dt><dd>Cabinetry, wainscot, porch floor, ceiling</dd><dt>Prep</dt><dd>Degloss, sand, bonding primer</dd><dt>Finish</dt><dd>Satin enamel, porch and floor enamel</dd>
project-built-ins-and-porch.html.palette:
Slate#5B6675
Wall white#F1F0EC
Porch grey#9EA3A2
Taupe#6E655B
text: Built-ins are furniture. They get sanded between coats, sprayed or laid off with a fine brush, and cured properly before anything goes back on the shelves.
Outside, the porch floor got a hand-laid diamond pattern in two greys under a bright white beadboard ceiling.

project-dealership.html.title: Auto Dealership
project-dealership.html.lede: A storefront that has to look sharp every day, finished on a schedule that kept the lot open.
project-dealership.html.facts: <dt>Location</dt><dd>Chittenden County</dd><dt>Type</dt><dd>Commercial, exterior</dd><dt>Surfaces</dt><dd>Metal panel, canopy, soffit</dd><dt>Prep</dt><dd>Degrease, scuff, metal primer</dd><dt>Finish</dt><dd>Industrial enamel</dd>
project-dealership.html.palette:
Clean white#F2F3F2
Signal red#C1272D
Silver panel#B9BEC3
Charcoal#3B3F44
text: Commercial exteriors are judged from the road at forty miles an hour and from the front door up close. We worked in sections and off-hours so sales never stopped.
Metal panels, canopy fascia and the soffit were all prepped and coated for a clean, even finish.

project-lake-cottage.html.title: Lake Cottage
project-lake-cottage.html.lede: A lakeside camp in a deep lake blue, with white rails and a screened porch ready for another fifty summers.
project-lake-cottage.html.facts: <dt>Location</dt><dd>Lake Champlain</dd><dt>Type</dt><dd>Residential, exterior</dd><dt>Surfaces</dt><dd>Clapboard, porch, rails, deck</dd><dt>Prep</dt><dd>Wash, scrape, board repair, prime</dd><dt>Finish</dt><dd>Satin body, gloss rails</dd>
project-lake-cottage.html.palette:
Lake blue#4F6F93
White trim#F1F1EE
Metal roof#A9AEB0
Deck grey#8A8C86
text: Lake houses take a beating from sun, wind and water. We stripped back failing paint, replaced and primed soft boards, and chose a coating built for exposure off the lake.
The result is a cottage that looks freshly built from the water and from the road, with rails and porch details picked out in white.

project-library.html.title: Library & Community Hall
project-library.html.lede: Bright walls, clean lines against exposed timber, and an open stair finished to gallery standard.
project-library.html.facts: <dt>Location</dt><dd>Greater Burlington</dd><dt>Type</dt><dd>Commercial, interior</dd><dt>Surfaces</dt><dd>Walls, ceilings, stair, restrooms</dd><dt>Prep</dt><dd>Patch, sand, prime new drywall</dd><dt>Finish</dt><dd>Scrubbable eggshell walls</dd>
project-library.html.palette:
Gallery white#EDEEEB
Ash timber#D9BE97
Black steel#1E1F1E
Fieldstone#A69E8E
text: Public buildings need durable finishes and a crew that works around people. We sequenced rooms so the building could stay in use, and kept the timber ceilings and stone untouched.
Walls and ceilings were finished in a scrubbable low-sheen white that makes the wood and daylight do the work.

project-queen-anne-victorian.html.title: Queen Anne Victorian
project-queen-anne-victorian.html.lede: Layers of spindles, brackets and fish-scale shingle, each one scraped, primed and cut in by hand.
project-queen-anne-victorian.html.facts: <dt>Location</dt><dd>Greater Burlington</dd><dt>Type</dt><dd>Residential, exterior</dd><dt>Surfaces</dt><dd>Clapboard, shingle, porch, trim</dd><dt>Prep</dt><dd>Lead-safe scrape, sand, prime, caulk</dd><dt>Finish</dt><dd>Satin body, semi-gloss trim</dd>
project-queen-anne-victorian.html.palette:
Cream siding#E6D9A8
White trim#F4F2EA
Slate blue#3F5D7A
Slate roof#8D9196
text: Queen Anne houses reward patience. Every bracket, baluster and band of trim is its own small project, and the paint has to sit cleanly on wood that has seen a century of Vermont winters.
The crew worked lead-safe from the first scrape, kept the porch usable for the family throughout, and finished with a layered scheme that reads cleanly from the street and up close.

project-red-shingle-colonial.html.title: Red Shingle Colonial
project-red-shingle-colonial.html.lede: Cedar shingle in barn red, black shutters and white trim, cut in one window at a time.
project-red-shingle-colonial.html.facts: <dt>Location</dt><dd>Chittenden County</dd><dt>Type</dt><dd>Residential, exterior</dd><dt>Surfaces</dt><dd>Cedar shingle, trim, shutters</dd><dt>Prep</dt><dd>Wash, scrape, spot-prime</dd><dt>Finish</dt><dd>Flat body, satin trim, gloss shutters</dd>
project-red-shingle-colonial.html.palette:
Barn red#8E3B2C
Black shutter#24272A
White trim#F2F1EC
Grey door#BFC0BC
text: Shingle siding drinks paint. Getting even color across thousands of edges means back-brushing every course and keeping a wet line all the way across a wall.
Shutters came down, trim went back to bright white, and the house kept its classic New England face.

project-sigma-phi-house.html.title: Sigma Phi House
project-sigma-phi-house.html.lede: Four Corinthian columns, a full pediment and a fanlight entry, restored to read crisp against red brick.
project-sigma-phi-house.html.facts: <dt>Location</dt><dd>Burlington, VT</dd><dt>Type</dt><dd>Institutional, exterior</dd><dt>Surfaces</dt><dd>Columns, pediment, cornice, windows, door</dd><dt>Prep</dt><dd>Scrape, consolidate, spot-prime</dd><dt>Finish</dt><dd>Gloss trim, natural oak door</dd>
project-sigma-phi-house.html.palette:
Brick#7A3B2E
Column white#F2F0EA
Limestone#D9D2C3
Oak door#8A5A35
text: Classical trim is unforgiving. Capitals, dentils and the fanlight over the door all show every drip, so the work is slow, detailed and done from the right equipment.
We scheduled around a busy house, protected the marble steps and landscaping, and left the entry looking the way it was built to look.
